newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters says coalition decision for party MPs.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters says coalition decision for party MPs.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters said on Tuesday he would leave it to his caucus of MPs to choose a coalition partner between the conservative National Party and and the centre-left Labour Party.
Peters said he would not be expressing his own preference. He said the NZ First meeting to decide on the coalition deal was likely to take all day.
Asked if he was going to express his own personal preference, Peters said: "No, I'm not. We are going to have to live with it. It's going to be a party and caucus decision."
Asked if he would persuade his caucus one way or the other, he said: "No, I don't intend to do that. They will make the decision themselves."
Asked if the decision would go to a vote, Peters said: "I think we can work it out (without voting) but one can't be certain. It might be a vote."
He expected to hear around 11 a.m. (2200 GMT) whether Labour, in separate talks, had secured the backing of the left-wing Alliance for a Labour-NZ First coalition.
